purpose: The criterion R1 uses to pick a target-orthography spelling for a phone. It lives in DATA because it is a MEASURED choice, not a coding preference.
definition: joint, except a grapheme the two alphabets SHARE wins when it is itself read as this phone

why_the_others_were_rejected.forward: produced 'bekliyor'->'beclyyod' and 'bizi'->'bysy' because English spells the flap /ɾ/ as 'd' at 0.871 and /i/ as 'y' at 0.639
why_the_others_were_rejected.reverse: keeps only 2/13 shared letters that are already read correctly, and picks rare context-bound digraphs ('tʃ'->'tu' at 1.000, 'k'->'cc', 'ʒ'->'su')
why_the_others_were_rejected.joint: keeps 11/13 instead of 13/13 — the guard is what closes that gap

unreachable_meaning: English orthography carries no string a tokeniser reads as these phones. A FINDING about the TARGET orthography, not a defect to patch: A2 measured Italian at 55.1 % feature coverage for Turkish against English 39.1 %, so the respelling target is itself a measurable choice and stays open work.
